Subject: Curated capacity matrix & addon swap — AcmeHealth

Hi Dana / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per Samir's note, you want to explore swapping the Advanced Indexing addon for the Real‑time Embeddings pack and also evaluate a modest tier shift that smooths peak capacity while keeping monthly spend within ~10% of today's run rate.

Attached is the capacity matrix we discussed (acme_capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx) — it maps current usage by endpoint to suggested pool sizes and two alternative packing strategies. Quick asks so we can move fast:
- Can procurement confirm whether the priority is lowest steady-state cost or strict peak headroom?
- Do you need a formal quote that separates one‑time migration credits from recurring line items?
- If we hold pricing for 30 days while you review, would that be sufficient?

I'll loop Kimberly on the pricing options and Priya on entitlements/seat counts. If helpful, we can do a short follow-up on Thursday to walk the matrix.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Thanks Marcus — got the matrix and appreciate the breakdown. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Priority is minimizing recurring spend while keeping a 20% buffer for monthly spikes. Peak headroom can reduce a bit, but we need reliability for scheduled clinical workflows.
2) Procurement will need a quote that clearly separates recurring unit costs from migration credits and any first‑quarter promotional discount.
3) 30 days to review is fine, but we prefer a 2‑week internal window to get final signoff if possible.

I've attached our procurement requirements doc so you can ensure the quote includes the standard AML language and SOC2 evidence links. Samir will coordinate approvals on our side.

On timing — could you have an initial pricing sketch by EOD Thursday? We should be able to respond with our preferred option the following week.

Best,
Dana Ruiz
Head of Cloud Integrations | AcmeHealth
dana@acmehealth.com

Hi Dana — looping in the pricing options so procurement has something concrete to review. Based on the usage profile in Marcus's matrix, two viable configurations: 

Option A — Cost‑optimized (recommended if steady‑state cost is primary)
- Swap Advanced Indexing for Real‑time Embeddings pack (same monthly token allowance).
- Reduce dedicated pool peak capacity by 15% and apply KV cache to high‑freq endpoints.
- Expected recurring delta: -8% vs current.
- Migration credit: one‑time $10,000 to offset connector rework.

Option B — Headroom assurance (recommended if you need buffer for spikes)
- Keep Advanced Indexing for critical pipelines, move noncritical workloads to a lower‑priority pool.
- Increase burst capacity allocation by 10% (metered).
- Expected recurring delta: +6% vs current.
- Migration credit: one‑time $4,000.

Discount / promotional terms
- For Option A we can apply a 20% discount on the recurring differential for the first 3 months (applies to recurring portion only).
- Pricing hold: We can hold the above pricing for 14 days from quote issuance.

Attached: quote_ACME-1873_v3.pdf with line‑by‑line items and the migration credit. If you prefer we can split the quote into a separate SOW for migration work.

Next steps
1) Procurement: confirm which option you prefer and whether the migration SOW should be separate.
2) If Option A, procurement signs the quote and we set a migrate window (typically 2 weekends).
3) If you want a call to walk the quote, Marcus and I are free Thursday 9–11 PT.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Deal Strategy | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: quote_ACME-1873_v3.pdf (PDF, 46KB)
